evidence: (1) Gates carry no reward mass: task/tests/scoring.toml:1-3 '[gates] render = 0.0 constraints = 0.0'; [weights] (lines 5-8) list only functional 0.6/polish 0.2/visual 0.2; score.py:46 computes weighted only over weights, so gate dimensions never enter the sum. scoring.toml (sha256 95f70d6e...), test.sh (bd682592...) and tools/score.py (13de2b38...) are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff -q). (2) Gates apply before shaping: score.py:41 gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); :42 scored_ran requires gates_passed; :48 reward = 0.0 unless gates_passed and floors_passed; returns 1 on gate failure (:83). test.sh:212 removes stale scored output, :213 runs gates first, :217-222 exit 1 -> exit 0 without running the scored suite (detailed zero kept), other codes -> write_zero_reward; :224 scored suite only after; :227 any score.py failure -> zero. Gate criteria are single binary criteria with aggregation all_pass (gates/render/judge.toml:14-21, gates/constraints/judge.toml:38-45), so a gate dimension is 0 or 1. (3) Gates exclude convincing dead apps (REVIEW_POLICY): constraints gate requires a UI-created job + candidate read back as the Observer in an independent empty browser context and explicitly rejects 'A static seed response, a no-op success message, a browser-only save or a job-only app'; render gate requires a wrong-password refusal plus a real staff workspace, 'A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'. Both are grounded in public text (instruction.md:17 accounts/password; hireops_rules.md:27-31 job title/team/manager/places 1-50, candidate name/email/source), so a conforming app is not gated on hidden requirements. Each scored prompt repeats the backend gate and hard-zeros a blank/static shell (functional prompt.md:9-13 'gives every binary criterion 0'; polish prompt.md:12 'binary0 throughout'; visual prompt.md:12 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'), so even a gate-judge slip cannot let a dead app collect polish/visual. (4) Functional floor: [floors] functional = 0.05 (scoring.toml:10-11), strict '>' at score.py:47. Functional total weight computed with tomllib = 58.5 over 43 binary criteria, so clearing the floor needs > 2.925 weight of real behaviour. Weak-app walk-through: a gate-passing app with only sign-in + shared job/candidate creation earns roughly hro_add_candidate 0.5 (0.0085) and is zeroed; adding persistence with notes (hro_restart 1.5) and job validation (hro_job_open 0.5) gives 2.5/58.5 = 0.043, still zeroed; only adding another genuine rule (e.g. reorder 1.5 -> 0.068) clears it. Polish criteria (hro_pol_live_board, live_thread, earlier_place, failed_send, session_resume) all require live/concurrent functionality, so they are not farmable by a static app. (5) Local measurement of the shipped score.py + scoring.toml (copied to scratchpad, synthetic RewardKit outputs; evidence/43 not needed): render=0 with perfect scored -> exit 1, reward 0.0000, weighted 0.0; gates pass, functional 0.05, polish 1, visual 1 -> reward 0.0000 (floors_passed 0, weighted 0.43); gates pass, scored missing -> 0.0000; gates missing a key -> exit 2 (test.sh writes plain zero); all 1 -> 1.0000. Risk=true because test.sh control flow and a gate-failing verifier run were not executed end to end (raw-evidence-index scope: 'reward discrimination/ranking ... are absent'), and a judge-level weak/dead-app run is unmeasured. Observation for rows 42/44 (template policy, not a task defect): an app just above the floor (functional 0.0598) with visual 1.0 and polish 0 scores 0.2359 in the local run, i.e. the template floor bounds but does not eliminate visual-only mass for a barely working app; this is template-controlled and outside task authority.
